'''Bob Jacklyn''' (January 13, 1922 – June 18, 2014) was an Australian cosmic ray physicist, and former head of the Australian Antarctic Division's research program.<ref name="Duldig01">{{cite journal|last1=Duldig|first1=M. L.|title=Australian Cosmic Ray Modulation Research|journal=Publications of the Astronomical Society of Australia|date=2001|volume=18|issue=1|pages=12–40|url=http://articles.adsabs.harvard.edu//full/2001PASA...18...12D/0000013.000.html|accessdate=13 January 2017|arxiv=astro-ph/0010147|bibcode=2001PASA...18...12D|doi=10.1071/AS01003|s2cid=12770429}}</ref> Mount Jacklyn, located in the [[Athos Range]] of Antarctica, is named after him for his important research at [[Mawson Station]] in 1956.<ref>{{cite web|title=Antarctica Detail|url=https://geonames.usgs.gov/apex/f?p=gnispq:5:0::NO::P5_ANTAR_ID:7427|website=U.S. Geological Survey|accessdate=25 September 2016}}</ref>

==Antarctic research==
Bob's team at [[Macquarie Island]] and [[Mawson Station]] provided new information about the nature and source of cosmic rays. Specifically, his team reaffirmed that the rays primary source was from 'storms' on the [[Sun]], and suggested that a small proportion of these rays had sidereal rather than solar periodicity. This important finding implied a Galactic or extra-galactic origin.<ref name="haynes2000">{{cite book|last1=Raymond|first1=Haynes|title=Explorers of the southern sky : a history of Australian astronomy|date=2000|publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]]|location=Cambridge, UK|isbn=9780521365758|page=326|edition=Reissue|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=XoeiJxMmXZ8C&pg=PA326|accessdate=13 January 2017}}</ref>
